source_text: λούσης αὐτὸ τῆς ἐν ἡμῖν νήψεως, καὶ ἀναιρούσης κατὰ βραχύ. Μόνορχιν δὲ πρὸς τούτοις, φησὶ, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τὸν ἡμίανδρον, καὶ οἱονεὶ παρακεκομμένον τὸ τελείως ἀνδροπρεπές. «Οὔτε γὰρ πόρνοι,» φησὶν, «οὔτε μαλακοὶ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ βασιλείαν κληρονομήσουσι.» Θηλυδρίας δὲ τοὺς τοιούτους ὀνομάζει, ὅτι τὴν ἀνδρὸς λαχόντες φύσιν, ψεύδονται τὸ ἀνδροπρεπὲς, καὶ νοῦν καὶ σῶμα μαλακιζόμενοι, καὶ ἑκοντὶ κατακλώμενοι πρὸς τὸ ἄναλκι καὶ θηλυπρεπές. Εἰκὸς δὲ δὴ πάλιν, τὸν μόνορχιν καὶ ἕτερόν τι παραδηλοῦν. Ἄνδρα μὲν γὰρ ὀνομάζειν ἔθος τὸν εὐσθενῆ καὶ συνεστραμμένον, καὶ οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχοντα πρὸς τὸ δύνασθαι κατορθοῦν ἃ ἂν ἕλοιτο τυχόν. Νοηθείη δ' ἂν εἰκότως ἐξ ἡμισείας ἀνὴρ, ὁ μὴ ὁλοκλήρως εὐσθενὴς, μήτε εἰσάπαν εἰς τὰ αὐτῷ πρέποντα γοργός· οὐ γάρ τοι προσήκει τὸν Θεῷ προσκείμενον, διακεκομμένην αὐτῷ τὴν ἀνδρείαν καὶ λελωβημένον προσάγειν τὸ εὐσθενὲς, καὶ ὡς ἀσθενεῖν ἐκ μέρους· ἀνδρίζεσθαι δὲ καὶ κραταιοῦσθαι, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, ἀδιάβλητον ἔχοντα καὶ ἀκατάσκωπτον προθυμίαν. Οὐκοῦν ἀνίερος μὲν ὁμολογουμένως, ὁ ὑπὸ μώμου γραφήν. Εἴργεται δὲ οὐχὶ τοῦ χρῆναι μεταλαχεῖν τῆς ἁγίας τροφῆς. «Φάγεται γὰρ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων,» φησὶ, «πλὴν πρὸς τὸ καταπέτασμα οὐ προσελεύσεται, καὶ πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον οὐκ ἐγγιεῖ» Οἱ γὰρ ἔτι ταῖς εἰς νοῦν ἔσω κεκρυμμέναις ἀσθενείαις ἔνοχοι, μεταλάχοιεν ἂν τῆς εὐλογίας Χριστοῦ, καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἐν τάξει τῇ τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἐπίδοσιν ἁγιασμοῦ, καὶ εἰς ἑδραιότητα νοῦ, καὶ τὴν ἐφ' ἅπασι τοῖς ἀρίστοις ἐρηρεισμένην διαμονὴν, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν τρόπῳ τῷ πρέποντι τοῖς ἠῤῥωστηκόσιν εἰς ἀπόθεσιν τοῦ κακοῦ, καὶ εἰς κατάληξιν ἁμαρτίας, καὶ εἰς νέκρωσιν ἡδονῶν, καὶ εἰς ἀνάληψιν εὐεξίας τῆς πνευματικῆς. Ἐπειδὴ γάρ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς καινὴ κτίσις, κατὰ τὰς Γραφὰς, ταύτῃτοι δεχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς διὰ τῆς ἁγίας αὐτοῦ σαρκός τε καὶ αἵματος, ἵνα πρὸς καινότητα ζωῆς ἀναστοιχειούμενοι δι' αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ, τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀποσκευαζώμεθα, τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀποφάσκει μὲν οὖν τῶν ἱερῶν ἔργων τὴν ἐπιτήδευσιν τοῖς οἱονείπως ἐντετηγμένην καὶ ἀναπόβλητον ἠῤῥωστηκόσι τὴν νοητὴν ἐπήρειαν· ἅγιον γὰρ ἥκιστά γε τὸ νοσοῦν ἀεὶ τὰ προσπεφυκότα τῶν παθῶν· ἀλλ' εἰ καί τινι [τῶν] ἀμωμήτως ἐχόντων ἔν γε δὴ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἀδιαβλήτως εἰς λειτουργίαν, τὸ ἀῤῥωστῆσαι συμβαίνει τὰ κοινὰ δὴ ταυτὶ καὶ οὐκ ἐξίτηλα τῶν παθῶν, οὐκ ἀνεπιτίμητον ἐᾶσθαι δεῖν αὐτὸν ἐπιτάττει, λέγων· «Εἶπον πρὸς Ἀαρὼν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσεχέτωσαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ οὐ βεβηλώσουσι τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ἅγιόν μου, ὅσα αὐτοὶ ἁγιάζουσί μοι· ἐγὼ Κύριος. Εἶπον αὐτοῖς· Εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν πᾶς ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἂν προσέλθῃ ἀπὸ παντὸς τοῦ σπέρματος
pass_a_gloss: [wrapping it round] the sobriety in us, and destroying it little by little. And one-testicled besides these, he says, as I think, the half-man, and as it were falsified in what is fully manly. 'For neither fornicators,' he says, 'nor soft men will inherit the kingdom of God.' He names such men effeminate, because, having received the nature of a man, they belie the manly, going soft in both mind and body, and willingly broken down to the feeble and womanish. And it is likely again that the one-testicled also hints at something else. For it is customary to name a man the one strong and compact, and not unable to accomplish what he may choose. A half-man would fittingly be understood as the one not wholly strong, nor fully vigorous for what befits him; for it is not fitting that the one attached to God bring a manliness cut through and a strength maimed, so as to be weak in part; but to play the man and be strong, according to what is written, having an eagerness blameless and not to be mocked. So unholy admittedly is the one under the written charge of blemish. Yet he is not barred from sharing the holy food. 'For he shall eat from the holy things,' he says, 'but he shall not come near to the veil, and shall not approach the altar.' For those still liable to weaknesses hidden within the mind might share in the blessing of Christ, and not as in the rank of the saints, for advance of sanctification, and for firmness of mind, and the abiding fixed in all the best things, but as in the manner fitting for the sick, for putting away the evil, and for ceasing of sin, and for putting to death of pleasures, and for regaining of spiritual good health. For since Christ is a new creation, according to the Scriptures, therefore we too receive him in ourselves through his holy flesh and blood, so that, being re-formed toward newness of life through him and in him, we may put off the old man, being corrupted according to the desires of deceit, according to what is written. PALL.: You spoke rightly. CYR.: So he denies the practice of the sacred works to those sick, as it were, with an ingrained and not-to-be-thrown-off spiritual affliction; for least holy is what is always sick with the passions grown onto it; but if to any of those who are blameless in themselves and unblamable in ministry it happens to be sick with these common and not fading of the passions, he commands that he must not be left unrebuked, saying: 'Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and let them keep away from the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they shall not profane my holy name, in whatever they themselves consecrate to me: I am the Lord. Say to them: Into your generations every man who comes near from all the seed
pass_b_english: Cyril: …in check and destroys it little by little. Next, as I at least think, he means by the man with only one testicle the half-man, the one who has, as it were, been cut off from full manliness. ‘For neither the sexually immoral,’ he says, ‘nor the soft will inherit the kingdom of God’ (1 Corinthians 6:9–10). By this he names the effeminate, because, though they were given the nature of a man, they belie their manhood: they grow soft in mind and body and willingly break themselves down into feebleness and womanish ways. It is likely, again, that the man with one testicle points to something else as well. For it is usual to call a ‘man’ one who is strong and well knit, and fully able to accomplish whatever he may choose. So a half-man may fittingly be understood as one who is not wholly strong, nor fully vigorous for what befits him. For it is not fitting that one devoted to God should bring him a courage cut short and a strength maimed, so as to be weak in part; rather he should ‘act like a man and be strong,’ as it is written (1 Corinthians 16:13), with an eagerness that no one can fault or mock. So the man listed under ‘blemish’ is admittedly unfit for sacred service. Yet he is not barred from sharing in the holy food. ‘For he shall eat of the holy things,’ he says, ‘but he shall not go in to the veil, and he shall not come near the altar’ (Leviticus 21:22–23). For those who are still subject to weaknesses hidden within the mind may share in the blessing of Christ, not as ranked among the saints, for growth in holiness, for steadiness of mind, and for a steadfastness firmly grounded in all that is best, but in the way that suits the sick: for the putting away of evil, the ending of sin, the putting to death of pleasures, and the recovery of spiritual health. For since Christ is a new creation, according to the Scriptures (2 Corinthians 5:17), we too therefore receive him into ourselves through his holy flesh and blood, so that, refashioned through him and in him for newness of life (Romans 6:4), we may put off the old man, who is being corrupted according to the desires of deceit, as it is written (Ephesians 4:22).

Cyril: So he forbids the practice of sacred duties to those who are sick with a spiritual affliction that is, as it were, ingrained and cannot be thrown off; for what is always sick with passions grown into it is not holy at all. But if one of those who are blameless in themselves and beyond reproach in their ministry happens to suffer these common passions, which do not fade away, he commands that he must not be left unrebuked, saying (Leviticus 22:2–3): ‘Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and let them keep away from the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they shall not profane my holy name in what they themselves consecrate to me: I am the Lord. Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man from all your offspring who comes near

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

1 Corinthians 6:9–10: μαλακοί rendered 'the soft' so that Cyril's next word, θηλυδρίας ('womanish'), reads as his own gloss on it. 'Act like a man and be strong' (ἀνδρίζεσθαι καὶ κραταιοῦσθαι) is cited as 1 Corinthians 16:13 (ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε); close parallels are Psalm 31:24 (LXX 30:25) and Deuteronomy 31:6. 'Christ is a new creation, according to the Scriptures' alludes to 2 Corinthians 5:17 (cf. Galatians 6:15), though Paul's text says that whoever is in Christ is a new creation. 'Newness of life' is Romans 6:4; 'the old man … corrupted according to the desires of deceit' is Ephesians 4:22 nearly verbatim. 'The blessing of Christ' (εὐλογία Χριστοῦ) is Cyril's usual term for the Eucharist, as the next sentence (his holy flesh and blood) shows; kept literal. 'Which do not fade away of themselves' renders οὐκ ἐξίτηλα (not fading, lasting); the sense seems to be passions that need cleansing rather than wearing off, but the phrase is doubtful against the contrast with 'ingrained' passions. 'Keep away from' renders προσεχέτωσαν ἀπό (LXX for Hebrew 'separate themselves from'). The quotation of Leviticus 22:2–9 runs on into section 8; the citation for its first part is placed at 'saying' because the quote stays open at the section break.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): [περιστελ]λούσης αὐτὸ τῆς ἐν ἡμῖν νήψεως (sobriety) καὶ ἀναιρούσης κατὰ βραχύ 'destroying little by little'. μόνορχις = ὁ ἡμίανδρος 'half-man', οἱονεὶ παρακεκομμένος τὸ τελείως ἀνδροπρεπές 'cut short of full manliness'. Quote οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε μαλακοὶ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ βασιλείαν κληρονομήσουσι. θηλυδρίας ὀνομάζει 'he names [them] womanish', because λαχόντες τὴν ἀνδρὸς φύσιν 'having obtained a man's nature' ψεύδονται τὸ ἀνδροπρεπές 'belie manliness', νοῦν καὶ σῶμα μαλακιζόμενοι 'softened in mind and body', ἑκοντὶ κατακλώμενοι 'willingly broken down' πρὸς τὸ ἄναλκι καὶ θηλυπρεπές 'to the feeble and womanly'. εἰκὸς the μόνορχις παραδηλοῦν 'indicates' another thing. ἄνδρα customary for τὸν εὐσθενῆ καὶ συνεστραμμένον 'strong and compact', οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχοντα to κατορθοῦν 'accomplish' what he chooses. ἐξ ἡμισείας ἀνήρ 'half-man' = one not ὁλοκλήρως εὐσθενής nor εἰσάπαν γοργός 'wholly vigorous' for τὰ πρέποντα. οὐ προσήκει τὸν Θεῷ προσκείμενον 'one devoted to God' διακεκομμένην ... τὴν ἀνδρείαν 'courage cut through' καὶ λελωβημένον τὸ εὐσθενές 'maimed strength' προσάγειν 'bring', ὡς ἀσθενεῖν ἐκ μέρους; but ἀνδρίζεσθαι καὶ κραταιοῦσθαι 'be manly and strong' as written, ἀδιάβλητον καὶ ἀκατάσκωπτον προθυμίαν 'unblameable, unmockable eagerness'. ἀνίερος ὁμολογουμένως 'admittedly unholy/unfit' ὁ ὑπὸ μώμου γραφήν 'the one listed under blemish'; οὐχὶ εἴργεται 'is not barred' from μεταλαχεῖν τῆς ἁγίας τροφῆς 'sharing the holy food'. Quote φάγεται ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων, πλὴν πρὸς τὸ καταπέτασμα (veil) οὐ προσελεύσεται, καὶ πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον οὐκ ἐγγιεῖ. Those still ἔνοχοι 'liable' to ἀσθένειαι hidden within the mind μεταλάχοιεν ἂν τῆς εὐλογίας Χριστοῦ 'may share the blessing (Eucharist) of Christ', not ἐν τάξει τῶν ἁγίων for ἐπίδοσις ἁγιασμοῦ 'increase of sanctification', ἑδραιότης νοῦ 'steadiness of mind', διαμονὴ ... ἐρηρεισμένη 'fixed continuance' in all τὰ ἄριστα, but ἐν τρόπῳ πρέποντι τοῖς ἠῤῥωστηκόσιν 'fit for the sick': εἰς ἀπόθεσιν τοῦ κακοῦ, κατάληξιν ἁμαρτίας, νέκρωσιν ἡδονῶν, ἀνάληψιν εὐεξίας πνευματικῆς 'recovery of spiritual fitness'. Since ὁ Χριστὸς καινὴ κτίσις κατὰ τὰς Γραφάς, δεχόμεθα αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς διὰ τῆς ἁγίας αὐτοῦ σαρκός τε καὶ αἵματος, ἵνα πρὸς καινότητα ζωῆς ἀναστοιχειούμενοι 'refashioned' δι' αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ, τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀποσκευαζώμεθα 'put off', τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης. PALL: ὀρθῶς ἔφης. CYR: ἀποφάσκει 'he forbids' τῶν ἱερῶν ἔργων τὴν ἐπιτήδευσιν 'practice of sacred works' to those sick with νοητὴν ἐπήρειαν 'spiritual affliction' οἱονεὶ ἐντετηγμένην 'melted in, ingrained' καὶ ἀναπόβλητον 'not to be cast off'; ἅγιον ἥκιστα τὸ νοσοῦν ἀεὶ τὰ προσπεφυκότα τῶν παθῶν 'grown-on passions'. But if to one ἀμωμήτως ἐχόντων 'blameless' in themselves and ἀδιαβλήτως εἰς λειτουργίαν, it happens ἀῤῥωστῆσαι τὰ κοινὰ ... καὶ οὐκ ἐξίτηλα τῶν παθῶν 'the common and not-fading passions', ἐπιτάττει 'he orders' that he not be left ἀνεπιτίμητον 'unrebuked', saying [Lev 22:2-3] εἶπον πρὸς Ἀαρὼν ... προσεχέτωσαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἁγίων 'let them keep from the holy things' ... οὐ βεβηλώσουσι τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ἅγιόν μου ... ἐγὼ Κύριος. εἶπον αὐτοῖς· εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἂν προσέλθῃ ἀπὸ παντὸς τοῦ σπέρματος [ὑμῶν in 8].

changes: θηλυδρίας δὲ τοὺς τοιούτους ὀνομάζει: Paul does not use 'womanish'; recast as 'By this he names the effeminate' so Cyril glosses Paul's μαλακοί
'a lasting stay firmly set' -> 'a steadfastness firmly grounded' (διαμονή, stiff)
οὐκ ἐξίτηλα: dropped the added 'of themselves'; now 'which do not fade away'

checked: 1 Corinthians 6:9-10, 1 Corinthians 16:13 (closest wording for ἀνδρίζεσθαι καὶ κραταιοῦσθαι), Leviticus 21:22-23, 2 Corinthians 5:17 allusion, Romans 6:4, Ephesians 4:22, Leviticus 22:2-3 LXX clause by clause
εὐλογία Χριστοῦ = Eucharist kept literal as 'the blessing of Christ'; doctrinal terms (flesh and blood, new creation) exact
